correctness.rationale: The metric restrictions follow by checking the source-pair triangles and the triangles with both added points. Average any operator over the actual block permutations and simultaneous block/center swap; this cannot increase the norm and leaves signed coefficients a,b with a+b=1/m. Boolean potentials force rC≥1−a and sC≥1−b; adding gives the mass term. The indicator of the rest of the near block also gives rC≥(m−1)a, yielding the saturation term. The whole-block indicator gives tC≥2ma−1; substituting a≥1−rC gives the interaction term. The signs of the coefficients were unrestricted in this argument. Conversely C equal to the four-term maximum makes a=max(1/(2m),1−rC) no greater than each of 1/m, sC−1+1/m, and (1+tC)/(2m). For the uniform branch the far-bound follows from s≥r and the mass bound; the other branch uses exactly the three nontrivial terms. Hence b=1/m−a is nonnegative, the source-to-center estimates follow by averaging differences, and the new-pair difference is (2ma−1) times the difference of block means, of norm at most (2ma−1)L for input seminorm L. This works in every real Banach space. Applying any universal extension guarantee to the canonical isometric embedding of X into its own free space gives by linearization a projection and by adjunction a scalar operator, so even a nonlinear choice cannot beat the factor. The one-center example has static max 6/5 and coupled max 4/3 at t=1/4; both phase thresholds follow by cross-multiplying positive denominators. Equalities in the metric constraints, including r=s, cause no degeneration except the excluded t=0.
residual_risks: The recorded 118 exact finite cases and separate 960-instance LP comparison are not independent all-parameter arguments; the latter is described but has no separate replay file in the supplied package. Neither is needed for the proof.

value.rationale: An exact relative projection/extension constant for this natural symmetric pair separates mass constraints visible to single-center tests from an obstruction visible only to simultaneous extension. The small strict example and sharp transition quantify when solving each one-center problem is insufficient for any Banach-valued extension scheme. This supplies a usable sharp benchmark, not merely an isolated numerical LP optimum.
residual_risks: The formula does not address unequal block sizes, nonequilateral sources, or larger added sets.
